fields.definition: Excitement, thrills, and high-energy action.
Suspense, dread, and the anticipation of conflict.
Moments of horror, shock, and startle-reflex.
The degree and visceral impact of physical conflict.
Feelings of love, affection, and romantic connection.
Sexual tension, sensuality, and explicit content.
Feelings of comfort, safety, and heartwarming positivity.
A sense of awe, amazement, or the sublime and magical.
The evocation of pity, tragedy, and profound sadness.
A sense of lingering sadness, pensive sorrow.
The unsettling feeling from things that are almost-human but not quite.
The feeling of emotional release, purification, or closure after experiencing intense drama.
A sentimental longing or wistful affection for a period in the past.
Humor derived from a consistent cast reacting to episodic, often formulaic, situations.
Clever dialogue, intellectual humor, and puns.
Slapstick, farcical situations, and action-based gags.
Humor from social awkwardness and uncomfortable situations.
Nonsensical, bizarre, or surreal comedy.
Critiquing society or other media through imitation and irony.
Comedy derived from morbid, taboo, or tragic subjects.
A world containing magic, mythical creatures, or non-historical lore.
A focus on science fiction, advanced technology, or future societies.
Set in and focused on a specific, real-world past era.
Set in the present day with a focus on believable situations and characters.
Centered on criminal acts, investigation, and the justice system.
A focus on solving a specific puzzle or uncovering a central unknown.
Centered on military conflict and its consequences.
A focus on governance, power structures, and political maneuvering.
Centered on competitive sports, including athletics, racing, or games.
The depiction of the life of a real person.
A focus on a character's transition from youth to adulthood.
A focus on blood-related or "found family" bonds, conflicts, and relationships.
A focus on internal struggles, mental states, and perception vs. reality.
Centered on the entertainment industry, including filmmaking, music, or theater.
Centered on video games, virtual reality, or other forms of interactive play.
A focus on contemporary pop culture, celebrity, or internet phenomena as a central theme.
The use of narrative to explicitly or implicitly critique societal norms.
A direct focus on economic disparity, class struggle, and the mechanics of capitalism.
The thematic exploration of how technology affects the human condition.
The exploration of faith, religion, or metaphysical concepts.
The quality of the story's construction—coherence, pacing, and setup/payoff.
The quality of the writing itself—how sharp, realistic, or poetic the dialogue is.
The nuance, development, and psychological realism of the characters.
A deliberately paced narrative that builds tension and character gradually.
A narrative with high-energy, rapid plot progression.
The power of the plot to hook the viewer and make them want to know what happens next.
The intricacy of the plot, number of characters, and interwoven storylines.
The likelihood of gaining more from subsequent viewings.
The degree to which the narrative has a positive or optimistic outlook.
The degree to which the narrative has a pessimistic, nihilistic, or tragic outlook.
The degree to which the narrative deliberately leaves elements open to interpretation.
Originality in concept, execution, or storytelling method.
The use of respectful tributes and "easter egg" references to other works.
Storytelling that does not follow a chronological sequence.
The use of self-referential storytelling or breaking the fourth wall.
The use of dream logic and bizarre, uncanny scenarios that challenge narrative reality.
A focus on bizarre characters or unconventional logic that requires cognitive adaptation.
The extent to which the work explicitly explores complex philosophical questions.
The extent to which the work imparts factual knowledge.
The quality of the overall creative vision and its execution.
The quality of the performances.
The art of visual storytelling, including camera work, color, and lighting.
The pacing, rhythm, and assembly of shots to create the final flow.
The quality of the original score.
How convincingly the production elements absorb the audience into the story's world.
The "wow factor" from large-scale visuals, action, or set pieces.
The degree of a unique, non-naturalistic visual or auditory style.
The intentional imitation of the artistic style of another work, artist, or genre.
An aesthetic characterized by hallucinatory, distorted, or highly vibrant sensory experiences.
The aesthetic use of biologically strange, body horror, or aesthetically repulsive imagery.
The use of theatricality, artifice, and a "so bad it's good" sensibility.
How crucial dialogue is to understanding and enjoying the work.
How crucial the score or soundtrack is to the emotional experience.
How crucial non-musical sound design is to the atmosphere and storytelling.
